source.title: Improved memory in recurrent neural networks with sequential non-normal dynamics

record.tranche_reason: Tests how recurrent-network initialization affects training outcomes on sequential tasks, extending initialization findings to vanilla RNNs and language modeling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation losses and successful-run counts for its own initializer experiments. Linear-decoding results use untrained networks; cited results from other studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests initialization-dependent trainability in a new setting: recurrent networks on long-memory tasks. Appendix C also directly tests an RNN adaptation of dynamical-isometry initialization. These bear on V4's initialization principle, but do not establish its specific feedforward depth or orthogonal-versus-Gaussian claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct but incomplete. The authors conclude that sequential non-normal initializers improve vanilla RNN performance and that training induces related structures even from orthogonal initialization. Uniform chain initialization does not directly improve LSTMs, but incorporating different learned structural patterns into different gates improves character-level language-model test performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares recurrent-network initializers, including non-normal chain motifs and normal identity or orthogonal initializers; it does not test the CIFAR classification recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and architecture: advantages vary across copy, addition, psMNIST, language modeling, and vanilla RNN versus LSTM.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla RNN initializers produce different final language-model test losses, with feedback chain lowest on all three benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequential non-normal initialization can improve vanilla RNN language-model test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Chain initialization does not improve LSTM test performance over orthogonal initialization; a gate-specific mixed initializer improves character-level PTB and enwik8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benefits of sequential initialization depend on recurrent architecture and gate-specific structure.

fits_no_version.finding: All four psMNIST models beat random-classifier loss after the first epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These small recurrent models learn useful psMNIST predictions under all four tested initialization families.

record.problems: For several benchmark comparisons, exact successful-run counts or loss values appear only in figures or tables; some conclusions depend on selected validation-loss thresholds and hyperparameter searches. The paper reports validation and test losses, not training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for untrained linear-decoding simulations, which do not measure trained-model outcomes. Figure-only aggregate trajectories and additional appendix sensitivity plots are not separately enumerated.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks reaching near-zero CIFAR training classification error, including corrupted labels.
Spurious local minima and extra student width in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation in plain convolutional networks and its prevention by identity residual shortcuts.

Feedforward trainable-depth comparisons; orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks; 10,000-layer convolutional training; direct measurement of training gradients. Fixed-length recurrent tasks do not establish greater trainable feedforward depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability training.
Batch normalization, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: The authors' own critical-initialization experiment: a tanh RNN modeled on Pennington et al.'s dynamically isometric example could not be trained successfully on copy or addition. Record the tested initialization, both tasks, and the qualitative failure; no numerical failure criterion is supplied for this experiment.

record.verdict_notes: Validation-loss success on recurrent tasks supports a restricted extension of V4. Final test-loss rankings alone do not support its training-speed or trainable-depth claims. No results challenge V4's specific feedforward orthogonal-versus-Gaussian prediction.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, and model size or training duration effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and extra student width.
Plain versus residual feedforward networks and the effects of depth, shortcuts, or normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient preservation across layers, plain feedforward network depth, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence.
Batch normalization and its effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: Chain

conditions.value: validation loss below 50% of loss for a baseline random model

Its values are supplied: orthogonal/chain/plain/mixed are 5.937/5.935/5.949/5.944 on PTB word, 1.230/1.230/1.245/1.227 on PTB character, and 1.583/1.586/1.584/1.577 on enwik8. Split by task and initializer if retaining these performance results.

relationships.reason: R1-R4 show initialization-dependent trainability: chain achieves 46/462 copy successes versus zero for normal initializers, and Appendix C reports rapid attainment of very small copy and addition losses with selected non-normal configurations.
relationships.display_finding: Chain initialization achieved 46/462 copy successes versus zero for normal initializers, and selected non-normal configurations rapidly attained very small copy and addition losses.
